Let the side lengths be \(a,b,c,d,e\) in order.  
For an equiangular pentagon the directions of the sides differ by \(72^{\circ}\);  
if we let  

\[
\omega = e^{i72^{\circ}}=\cos 72^{\circ}+i\sin 72^{\circ},
\]

then  

\[
a+b\omega+c\omega^{2}+d\omega^{3}+e\omega^{4}=0          \tag{1}
\]

(the vector sum of the sides must be zero).

---

### 1.  Diagonal lengths

The diagonal joining the ends of sides \(a\) and \(b\) has vector  
\(a\cdot 1 + b\omega\); hence

\[
\text{(diag)}^{2}=|a+b\omega|^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}+2ab\cos 72^{\circ}.
\]

Thus for the five diagonals

\[
\sum (\text{diag})^{2}= \sum (s_i^{2}+s_{i+1}^{2})+2\cos 72^{\circ}\sum s_is_{i+1}.
\]

Since \(\sum s_i^{2}=308\),

\[
\sum (\text{diag})^{2}=2\cdot308+2\cos 72^{\circ}\,S=800,
\]

where \(S=\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{5}s_i s_{i+1}\) (adjacent products).  
Because \(\cos72^{\circ}= \dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{4}\),

\[
616+2\!\left(\frac{\sqrt5-1}{4}\right)S=800
\Longrightarrow
S=\frac{184}{2\cos72^{\circ}}=92(\sqrt5+1).      \tag{2}
\]

---

### 2.  Using the closure condition

From (1) we have  

\[
\sum_{i=1}^{5}s_i^{2}+2\sum_{1\le i<j\le5}s_i s_j\cos\bigl((j-i)72^{\circ}\bigr)=0 .
\]

There are five adjacent pairs (\(\cos72^{\circ}\)) and five non‑adjacent pairs
(\(\cos144^{\circ}=-\cos36^{\circ}\)).  Let  

\[
T=\sum_{i=1}^{5}s_i s_{i+2}
\]

(the products of sides two apart).  
Since \(\cos36^{\circ}= \dfrac{\sqrt5+1}{4}\),

\[
308+2\bigl(\cos72^{\circ}\,S-\cos36^{\circ}\,T\bigr)=0.
\]

Insert (2) and solve for \(T\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
2\cos72^{\circ}S&=2\!\left(\frac{\sqrt5-1}{4}\right)92(\sqrt5+1)=184,\\
T&=\frac{308+184}{2\cos36^{\circ}}
    =\frac{492}{\,2\cdot\frac{\sqrt5+1}{4}}
    =246(\sqrt5-1).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]

---

### 3.  The perimeter

Let \(p=a+b+c+d+e\) be the perimeter.  Then  

\[
p^{2}= \sum s_i^{2}+2\!\sum_{i<j}s_i s_j
      =308+2\,(S+T).
\]

From (2) and (3),

\[
S+T=92(\sqrt5+1)+246(\sqrt5-1)=338\sqrt5-154.
\]

Hence  

\[
p^{2}=308+2(338\sqrt5-154)=676\sqrt5.
\]

Thus the square of the perimeter is \(676\sqrt5\), i.e. \(m=676\) and
\(n=5\).  Consequently  

\[
m+n = 676+5 = 681.
\]

\[
\boxed{681}
\]
